correctness.rationale: A complete graph classification proves the independence polynomial for every finite commutative local ring with residue characteristic >=5: two exceptional components; (M−1)/2 paths generated by paired nonzero radical elements; δ/2 simple-root edges lifted uniquely through the nilpotent radical; remaining six-cycles under the S3 action. Products of component polynomials give the claimed coefficients, extremal size and exact leading coefficient. Computational checks independently reconstruct graph components and coefficients but are not used to prove the universal theorem.

value.rationale: Recent prime-field sum-product-avoidance research motivates understanding nonfield residue rings, where zero divisors change connected components. A complete size-distribution enumerator for every finite commutative local ring of residue characteristic >=5, with new path factors and ring-invariant exact counts, addresses a natural structural enumerative problem and distinguishes same-order fields from nonfields.
